extracted.intended_audience: general readers, AI researchers/practitioners, policymakers, educators, and legal professionals interested in AI hallucination
extracted.subtask_description: Summarize criteria, causes, classifications, impacts, and mitigation/detection techniques for AI 'hallucinations' (false or ungrounded AI outputs) across modalities and domains. Includes evaluative dimensions (factuality, grounding, robustness), mitigation approaches (data/modeling/retrieval/post-processing), and domain-specific safeguards (human review, citation auditing).

rubrics_metrics.name: Factuality / Accuracy / Groundedness
rubrics_metrics.description: A hallucination is a response generated by AI that contains false or misleading information presented as fact; often defined as 'generated content that appears factual but is ungrounded'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detecting and mitigating errors and hallucinations is essential for reliable deployment in high-stakes scenarios (chip design, supply chain, medical diagnostics). Examples include fabricated facts, invented quotations, and non-existent citations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intrinsic versus Extrinsic Hallucination (Grounding relative to source)
rubrics_metrics.description: Classification depending on whether the output contradicts the source (intrinsic) or cannot be verified from the source (extrinsic).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this distinction to evaluate whether a model's output is unfaithful to a provided source text or simply unverifiable from it; different mitigation/detection methods may be needed per type.

rubrics_metrics.name: Closed-domain versus Open-domain Hallucination (Prompt consistency)
rubrics_metrics.description: Depending on whether the output contradicts the prompt (closed-domain) or not (open-domain).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This categorization helps assess whether hallucination arises from prompt mismatch or from unconstrained generation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Source-reference fidelity / Source-reference divergence
rubrics_metrics.description: Hallucination may arise as an artifact of heuristic data collection or tasks where training data exhibit source-reference (target) divergence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate dataset construction and alignment between sources and targets; reduce divergence through careful dataset curation and annotation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training / Data Quality and Representativeness
rubrics_metrics.description: Incomplete, inaccurate or unrepresentative datasets can cause hallucinations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mitigation includes building faithful datasets, cleaning data automatically, and augmenting inputs with external information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data Preprocessing Fidelity (e.g., OCR transcription losses)
rubrics_metrics.description: Errors introduced when transcribing data (e.g., OCR) can lose structured information and introduce inaccuracies that lead to hallucination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess and improve transcription pipelines; validate converted text against originals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective / Modeling Incentives (next-word prediction encourages guessing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Pre-training objectives (predict-next-word) incentivize models to 'give a guess' even when lacking information, leading to hallucinations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider altering training/objective design or fine-tuning to reward uncertainty acknowledgment rather than guessing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Memorization and Overconfidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Models can memorize knowledge in parameters and be overconfident in incorrect memorized content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate how memorized parameters are relied upon; use retrieval or uncertainty methods to avoid overconfident false assertions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decoder/Decoding Strategy Effects (sampling impacts hallucination)
rubrics_metrics.description: Decoding strategies that increase diversity (e.g., top-k sampling) are positively correlated with increased hallucination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose decoding strategies mindful of the trade-off between diversity/creativity and factuality; consider deterministic or constrained decoding for high-stakes outputs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attention / Encoder-Decoder Alignment
rubrics_metrics.description: Errors in encoding/decoding and attending to wrong parts of the input can produce unfaithful generations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyze attention alignment and encoder representations; architectural changes can reduce mis-attention-driven hallucinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Novelty versus Usefulness Tradeoff
rubrics_metrics.description: A focus on novelty in model outputs may yield original but inaccurate responses, while focus on usefulness may yield memorized content lacking originality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance creative generation and factual reliability according to application needs; tune models and evaluation metrics accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretability / Internal Safety Circuits
rubrics_metrics.description: Internal circuits (e.g., that inhibit answering unless the model 'knows' the answer) can fail and lead to hallucinations when mis-inhibited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpretability research can identify and fix circuits responsible for unsafe or overconfident outputs; consider circuit-level interventions for safety.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adversarial Robustness
rubrics_metrics.description: Adversarial inputs can cause 'adversarial hallucinations' where models detect nonexistent objects or produce erroneous outputs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Test systems against adversarial attacks; apply adversarial training and robustness evaluations especially for vision and safety-critical systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modality-specific Accuracy
rubrics_metrics.description: Hallucination is not limited to text; image, audio, and object-detection modalities have their own hallucination failure modes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate and mitigate hallucinations per modality (text-to-image, TTS, object detection), using modality-appropriate tests and defenses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation and Reference Integrity
rubrics_metrics.description: LLMs frequently fabricate references, DOIs, or misattribute authors and content, producing nonexistent or incorrect citations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require verification of any AI-provided citations; for academic/scientific use, avoid trusting generated references without manual vetting; publishers may set policies discouraging AI-generated citations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human Verification Requirement for High-stakes Domains
rubrics_metrics.description: Courts and professional settings have required human review of AI outputs before submission (e.g., banning unreviewed AI-generated briefs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt mandated human verification for legal, medical, and other high-stakes outputs to prevent submission of fabricated facts or case law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uncertainty Quantification and Confidence Estimation
rubrics_metrics.description: Model uncertainty estimation techniques can be applied to detect hallucinations, especially when external data sources are absent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement calibrated confidence scores; use uncertainty-aware generation policies and surface uncertainty to users.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounding via External Knowledge / Retrieval (RAG / path grounding)
rubrics_metrics.description: Grounding LLM responses in factual data using external knowledge sources (retrieval-augmented generation, path grounding) reduces hallucinations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incorporate retrieval systems, validate retrieved sources, and prefer grounded answers for factual queries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Knowledge- and Retrieval-based Approaches
rubrics_metrics.description: Approaches that ground responses in external knowledge (retrieval, path grounding) are categorized as knowledge/retrieval methods for mitigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine retrieval with model generation; evaluate retrieval coverage and freshness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Model Architecture and Training Interventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Mitigation methods include architecture changes (encoder/attention/decoder), fine-tuning (including RLHF), and anti-hallucination fine-tuning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply targeted architectural and training modifications and evaluate their effect on factuality across tasks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-processing and Output Correction
rubrics_metrics.description: Post-processing methods can detect and correct hallucinations in outputs after generation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use filters, validators, or secondary models to flag or rewrite dubious content before presenting to users.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-category Mitigation Taxonomy (data-related vs modeling/inference)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ji et al. divide mitigation methods into data-related methods (dataset construction, cleaning, augmentation) and modeling/inference methods (architectural changes, training, post-processing).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose mitigation strategies according to this taxonomy; combine data improvements with modeling fixes for best results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Targeted Mitigation by Hallucination Type
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation and mitigation can focus on specific hallucination types (e.g., quantity/entity errors in summarization; self-contradiction).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design evaluation metrics and mitigation tailored to the hallucination subtype being addressed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multi-agent Consensus / Debate
rubrics_metrics.description: Getting different chatbots to debate one another until they reach consensus has been proposed as a mitigation method.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use multi-agent techniques to surface disagreements; note increased computational cost and potential for collusion or common-mode errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Neuro-symbolic and Logic-based Architectures
rubrics_metrics.description: Neuro-symbolic architectures that reason in formal logic are proposed to reduce hallucinations by introducing symbolic reasoning constraints.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Integrate symbolic reasoning modules or logic-based checks where possible to verify claims that require formal correctness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Web-search Validation of Low-confidence Generations
rubrics_metrics.description: Actively validate model-generated statements (especially low-confidence ones) using web search results and create validation questions checked via APIs (e.g., Bing search API).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use search-backed verification and logical rules based on page rank/hierarchy to confirm or reject generated claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-phase Detection Frameworks (unsupervised screening + LLM validation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Detect hallucinations via a two-phase approach: unsupervised screening then LLM-based validation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ unsupervised anomaly detection to flag candidates, followed by validation steps to reduce false positives/negatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guardrails / Hard-coded Response Rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Tools such as Nvidia Guardrails can be configured to hard-code certain responses instead of leaving them to the LLM.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define explicit constraints for disallowed outputs or canonical safe replies to avoid risky generation in known failure modes.

rubrics_metrics.name: External Detection Tools and Services
rubrics_metrics.description: Tools like SelfCheckGPT, Trustworthy Language Model, and Aimon have emerged to detect hallucinations in experimentation and production.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Integrate detection tools into development and production pipelines; validate tool performance on domain-specific data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assigning Confidence Scores and Evaluating Multiple Candidates
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluating multiple possible replies and assigning confidence scores before answering could mitigate hallucinations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trade-offs include increased compute and latency; necessary in high-stakes applications despite costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Active Learning and Cost-Accuracy Trade-offs
rubrics_metrics.description: Active learning and other mitigation techniques increase computational costs; in high-stakes domains such costs may be operationally necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Weigh operational cost vs required safety; implement more expensive mitigations for critical applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Benchmark and Evaluation Design (rewarding uncertainty over guessing)
rubrics_metrics.description: OpenAI researchers proposed changing benchmark scoring to discourage guessing and instead reward acknowledging uncertainty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Redesign evaluation metrics to penalize confident falsehoods and reward calibrated uncertainty and factual grounding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional Policies, Citation Auditing and AI Literacy
rubrics_metrics.description: Academic publishers and institutions may implement policies (e.g., discouraging AI-generated citations), citation auditing, and AI literacy training to mitigate hallucination harms in education/research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt editorial policies, automated citation-checking tools, and training for students and researchers; librarians may need to audit references more frequently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terminology and Framing (avoid anthropomorphism)
rubrics_metrics.description: Some researchers criticize the term 'hallucination' for anthropomorphizing models and advocate careful linguistic practices and alternative terms (confabulation, fabrication, factual error).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose precise terminology when describing failure modes to avoid misleading users about models' cognitive status and to assign proper responsibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Domain-specific Consequence Assessment (legal, scientific, educational impacts)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess the downstream consequences of hallucinations in specific domains (e.g., fabricated case law in court filings, fabricated citations in scientific research, misinformation in education).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply stricter safeguards and verification in domains where hallucinations have serious legal, ethical, or safety consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Detection and Mitigation Focused on Self-contradiction and Quantity Errors
rubrics_metrics.description: Researchers propose specific methods to detect and mitigate self-contradictory statements and quantity/entity hallucinations in summarization and dialogue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include checks for internal consistency and specialized modules for numeric and factual quantity validation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation via Human and Automatic Detectors (limitations noted)
rubrics_metrics.description: AI-detection tools and human reviewers currently have limited accuracy (e.g., detectors and humans detect generated abstracts with ~66-68% accuracy).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine multiple detection approaches and do not rely solely on current detectors; expect false negatives/positives and validate critical outputs.
